title: India Summons Russia After Black Sea Missile Strike Kills Four Seafarers
excerpt: Russia hit the Mumbai-owned MV Golden Leo with cruise missiles near Odesa, killing four Indian crew members. New Delhi called the attack on commercial shipping deplorable.
body:
• Four Indian nationals were killed when Russian cruise missiles struck the MV Golden Leo, a grain cargo ship, near Odesa on July 19
  • India summoned Russian chargé d’affaires Vladimir Ladanov and condemned the attack as “deplorable” and a threat to maritime commerce
  • The Mumbai-owned vessel was carrying corn and had 17 crew members, including five Indians — one remains hospitalized in critical condition
  • The incident is part of a broader pattern: India has also lost seafarers in the Iran-US conflict and protested strikes by both sides

India summoned a senior Russian diplomat on Tuesday and delivered a sharp rebuke after a missile strike killed four Indian seafarers on a grain cargo ship in the Black Sea, marking one of the deadliest attacks on Indian commercial crew in the ongoing Ukraine war.

The MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel owned by Mumbai-based Ocean Grace Shipping Ltd, was hit by three Kh-59/Kh-69 cruise missiles on July 19 as it departed Odesa loaded with corn, according to Ukraine’s navy. The strike ignited a fire on the ship’s starboard superstructure, killing ten crew members — four Indians and six Syrians — out of the 17 aboard.

India’s Diplomatic Response

Vladimir Ladanov, Russia’s chargé d’affaires in New Delhi, was called to the Ministry of External Affairs and told that targeting commercial shipping was “unacceptable,” the ministry said in a statement.

“Such attacks undermine the safety, security, and stability of international maritime commerce.”

— India’s Ministry of External Affairs

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was in contact with India but defended the military action. “Our armed forces are striking — and will continue to strike — vessels involved in transporting ammunition, weapons, and so on for the purposes of the Kyiv regime,” Peskov told reporters. The Golden Leo was carrying corn, not military cargo.

A Growing Toll on Indian Seafarers

The Black Sea attack is the latest in a series of incidents that have put Indian merchant mariners at risk across multiple conflict zones. In June, three Indian sailors were killed when the US Navy struck the MT Settebello, a commercial tanker, in the Gulf of Oman. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar personally protested to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, calling the lethal action “not justified.”

On Friday, a Mozambique-flagged LPG tanker named Disha carrying 28 Indian crew members was attacked by an unknown missile near the Strait of Hormuz in Iranian territorial waters. All crew members were reported safe. India has also summoned Iranian diplomats after separate strikes on UAE-flagged tankers left one Indian dead.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

India supplies one of the world’s largest pools of commercial seafarers, with an estimated 240,000 Indians serving on merchant vessels globally. The escalating risks in the Black Sea, Persian Gulf, and Strait of Hormuz threaten not just individual lives but the livelihoods of entire coastal communities in Gujarat, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu that depend on maritime employment.

The Forward Seamen’s Union of India has called for enhanced safety protocols and insurance coverage for Indian crew members operating in conflict zones. Maritime industry groups have urged the Indian government to negotiate safe passage guarantees with all parties.

What’s Next

The Indian mission in Ukraine is closely monitoring the condition of the fifth Indian crew member, who remains hospitalized in critical condition. The ministry has said it is working to repatriate the remains of the four deceased seafarers. Russia’s continued attacks on deepwater ports in southern Ukraine — which handle much of the country’s grain exports — show no signs of abating, raising the prospect of further risks to commercial shipping and their international crews.
